title.title: A superquadratic separation of sensitivity and block sensitivity
title.subtitle: Claim: Boolean functions with $\mathrm{bs}(f) \ge s(f)^\alpha$ for a fixed $\alpha > 2$

plain: Count single switches that flip a decision versus groups of switches: groups win by more than a square

beats.text: Sensitivity flips one bit at a time; block sensitivity flips disjoint blocks
Huang (2019) bounded block sensitivity by $s^4$; every example stayed quadratic
Claimed: functions beating quadratic by a fixed power

steps: Start from a small function where groups beat single flips
Plug copies of it into itself, level by level
Each level widens the gap, past the square

data.label: the gap grows with every level

achievement.label: Quadratic Sensitivity Conjecture (Nisan–Szegedy, 1994)
achievement.note: $\alpha$ is unspecified; the gap up to Huang's $s^4$ remains

verify.detail: SensitivitySeparation.lean, about 4.4k lines: the easiest claim here to audit
verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean or referee the proof

voice.text: Flip one bit or a group. Groups were thought to win by a square at most.
Nest a small function inside itself, and the gap grows each level.

sources.quote: Nisan-Szegedy (1994) asked whether bs <= s^2; Rubinstein (1995) quadratic separation
Huang (Annals 2019, arXiv 1907.00847) proved the Sensitivity Conjecture, giving bs <= s^4
alpha is some fixed constant >2, not specified as large
